For training routines it depends on your goals.

If it is strength then look at some power-lifting type stuff like Starting Strength or Strong Lifts.

For aesthetics then maybe something like Arnold Shwarzenegger 's Complete Guide to Body-building, which can at least tell you what muscles you are using for each exercise and has beginner routines.

I've lifted for a long time and never really done any specific routine, just learned slowly but surely from advice and mistakes. Good luck.
I am going to do the 3/2/1 method. I am going to focus on balance this year. For every push do a pull, train opposite muscles equally.

Just my two cents. Check out Russian kettlebells. If you really want to bulk up, it's not for you but if you want to work out everything from head to toe all at once, quickly, you may want to try it out. I started out in July with one kettlebell and have since added another. No gym membership required. I started out with the book, "Kettlebells for Dummies" and have added a couple more books since then. I've been more than happy with the results so far. I'm 61, by the way.
